mainTopic: Wine and character; which תנא רב's courtyard ruling follows; renting a גוי's rights from a landlord and on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching that wine flowing freely in a home is a sign of ברכה. רבי אילעאי adds that a person's true character shows in his cup, his pocket and his anger, and some add his laughter. The גמרא then returns to עירובין with רב's case: a Jew and a גוי live in an inner courtyard, a Jew lives in the outer one, and carrying is forbidden. The גמרא tests which תנא רב follows. It rejects רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, then challenges רבי עקיבא's rule of the 'foot'. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע settles it: רב follows both רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי עקיבא, in a case where the two Jews made an עירוב, so only the גוי forbids. רבי אליעזר asks about the reverse case, with the גוי in the outer courtyard, and רב rules strictly. Two inn stories follow about renting a גוי's rights: from a landlord when the tenant is away, which רבי אפס approves, and on שבת itself, which the Sages dispute. In the second story the Sages bring the question to רבי יוחנן, whose answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Wine flowing like water is a sign of blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a teaching from the previous lines: if wine flows freely in a person's house, that house has ברכה, and if not, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If wine is poured out in his house like water, there is blessing; and if not, there is no blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an aggadic teaching that began on the previous amud. Wine flowing freely in a home is a sign that the home is blessed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is the end of a דרשה about wine and blessing. The test is simple: plenty of wine, like water, means ברכה; a lack of it means no ברכה. It closes that short aggadic thread before the next teaching.

phrases.english: If [wine] flows in his house like water —
phrases.notes: The subject (wine) comes from the teaching on the previous amud.

phrases.english: there is blessing,
and if not — [there is] not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נִשְׁפָּךְ בְּבֵיתוֹ כַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the aggadic teaching about wine that began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Plenty of wine in a home, flowing like water, is a sign of ברכה.

steps.title: A person's character shows in three things
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעאי teaches that a person's real nature is revealed through his cup, his pocket and his anger. Others add his laughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעאי said: A person is recognized by three things: his cup, his pocket, and his anger. And some say: also by his laughter.
steps.whatsHappening: Staying with the topic of wine, רבי אילעאי gives a teaching about how you can tell what a person is really like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three tests are how he acts when he drinks (בכוסו), how he deals with money (בכיסו), and how he acts when angry (בכעסו). In these moments people show who they truly are. A second opinion adds a fourth test: how and at what he laughs (בשחקו).

keyTerms.meaning: in his pocket (how he handles money)

steps.whatToRemember: כוסו, כיסו, כעסו — and some add שחקו. These are the moments when a person's true self shows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elai said,
By three things a person is recognized:
by his cup, by his pocket, and by his anger.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: כוס, כיס and כעס sound alike.

phrases.english: And some say: also by his laughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַאי, בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָדָם נִיכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the wine theme with a teaching about drinking and character.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's character is revealed through his drinking, his money dealings and his anger. Some add his laughter.

steps.title: רב's case of a Jew and a גוי in the inner courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב reports a case: a Jew and a גוי lived in an inner courtyard, and a Jew lived in the outer courtyard. Both רבי and רבי חייא forbade carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: [There was a case of] a Jew and a גוי in the inner courtyard, and a Jew in the outer courtyard. The case came before רבי, and he forbade [carrying]; and before רבי חייא, and he forbade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the laws of עירובין. It brings a real case that came before two great authorities, and both of them forbade carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner courtyard's residents must walk through the outer courtyard to reach the street, so the two courtyards affect each other. The גוי living in the inner courtyard causes a problem. Both רבי and רבי חייא ruled that carrying is forbidden unless the Jews rent the גוי's rights.
steps.confusionAlert: The people of the inner courtyard pass through the outer courtyard. That is why a גוי living only in the inner courtyard can still affect carrying in the outer one.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A Jew and a non-Jew in the inner [courtyard],
and a Jew in the outer [courtyard].
The case came before Rabbi, and he forbade [carrying],
phrases.notes: רבי means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and before Rabbi Chiya, and he forbade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹי בַּפְּנִימִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic material and returns to the halachic topic of עירובין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this courtyard arrangement, carrying is forbidden without renting the גוי's rights. Both רבי and רבי חייא ruled this way.

steps.title: רב ששת asks whose view רב's ruling follows
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף are sitting at the end of רב ששת's lecture. רב ששת asks which תנא רב's ruling follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף were sitting at the end of רב ששת's lecture. רב ששת sat and said: According to whom did רב say his ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene and asks a question. It wants to know which earlier opinion is the basis for רב's ruling. This step prepares the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known מחלוקת about whether a גוי can forbid carrying for a single Jew who lives with him. To understand רב's ruling, we need to know which side he follows. The question כמאן means 'like whom?'

keyTerms.meaning: at the end of his lecture

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef were sitting
at the end of Rav Sheshet's lecture,
and Rav Sheshet sat and said:
According to whom did Rav say his ruling?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אַמְרַהּ רַב לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling reported in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion is the basis for רב's ruling forbidding carrying?

steps.title: It follows רבי מאיר, and רבה nods
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that רב's ruling follows רבי מאיר. רבה nods his head in agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר. רבה nodded his head.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers his own question: רב follows רבי מאיר. רבה shows that he agrees by nodding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a גוי forbids carrying even for a single Jew who lives with him, so the Jew must rent the גוי's rights. That would explain why רבי and רבי חייא forbade carrying here. רבה's nod shows that he agreed, and in the next step רב יוסף will challenge both of them for accepting this explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: Linking רב to רבי מאיר tells us where the ruling stands in the larger מחלוקת. It also sets up the next part of the sugya, where רב יוסף challenges this attribution, which both רב ששת and רבה accepted.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir.
Rabba nodded his head.
phrases.notes: A sign of agreement. רב יוסף challenges this agreement in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר. כַּרְכֵּישׁ רַבָּה רֵישֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's ruling follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a גוי forbids carrying even for a single Jew. רבה nods in agreement.

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges the claim that רב follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks how such great scholars could make this mistake. Under רבי מאיר, mentioning a Jew in the outer courtyard would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Could two great men like these Sages make a mistake in such a matter? If the ruling follows רבי מאיר, why do I need a Jew in the outer courtyard?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the answer just given, that רב's ruling follows רבי מאיר. He asks why רב's case would bother to mention a Jew in the outer courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a גוי living in a courtyard forbids carrying even if only one Jew lives there with him. So under רבי מאיר, the inner courtyard alone would already be forbidden. The Jew in the outer courtyard would add nothing, yet רב's case clearly treats him as important.

keyTerms.meaning: Two great men (here, the great scholars who agreed to this answer)
Why do I need it? (a detail that seems unnecessary)

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not challenging רב's ruling itself. He is challenging רב ששת's explanation of which תנא the ruling follows.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Two great men like these Sages
phrases.notes: Refers to רבה and רב ששת, who agreed that רב follows רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: would they err in such a matter?
If it is like Rabbi Meir,
why do I need a Jew in the outer courtyard?
phrases.notes: Under רבי מאיר, one Jew living with a גוי is already forbidden to carry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: תְּרֵי גַּבְרֵי רַבְרְבֵי כְּרַבָּנַן לִיטְעוֹ בְּהַאי מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from step 5 that רב follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב's ruling follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי מאיר, the outer-courtyard Jew is a pointless detail, yet רב's case includes him as if he matters.

steps.title: Possible defense: the case simply happened that way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a defense. Maybe the outer Jew is mentioned only because that is how the real-life case happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the incident that happened, happened this way (so the outer Jew is just a detail of the story)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way to save the רבי מאיר explanation. It is setting this answer up so that it can knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the Jew in the outer courtyard is not legally important. He appears only because the people who asked the question described every detail of their real situation. If so, his mention would not disprove רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer that is about to be rejected)
The incident happened this way (a detail recorded because it was part of the actual story)

phrases.english: And if you say,
the incident that took place, took place this way,
phrases.notes: Meaning the outer Jew was mentioned only as part of the real story.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיָה כָּךְ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to רב יוסף's challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The detail is explained as a fact of the story, not a legal requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer Jew seemed necessary for the prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps he is just a story detail, so רבי מאיר can still work.

steps.title: But רב himself permitted the inner Jew to carry
steps.stepSummary: The defense fails. רב was asked whether the inner Jew may carry in his own courtyard, and he said it is permitted. That goes against רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't they ask רב: What is the law for the inner one in his own place? And he said to them: It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense from the last step. It proves from רב's own words that he does not hold like רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that the Jew in the inner courtyard may carry in his own courtyard, even though a גוי lives there with him. Under רבי מאיר, the גוי would forbid him even there. So רב clearly disagrees with רבי מאיר. The outer Jew must therefore be the real reason for the prohibition, not just a story detail.

keyTerms.meaning: The one in the inner courtyard
In his own place (his own courtyard)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב's prohibition only applies to the outer courtyard. The inner Jew is fine in his own courtyard, so the question becomes why the outer Jew is forbidden.

phrases.english: But didn't they ask Rav:
What is the law for the inner one in his own place?
phrases.notes: May the Jew in the inner courtyard carry in his own courtyard?

phrases.english: And he said to them: It is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב: פְּנִימִי בִּמְקוֹמוֹ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the defense offered in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that רב follows רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב permits a single Jew living with a גוי to carry in his own courtyard, which רבי מאיר forbids.

steps.title: Could רב follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב? No
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests whether רב follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. It rejects this, because he requires two Jews in the same courtyard who forbid each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what? Does it follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב? But he said: a גוי does not forbid unless there are two Jews who forbid carrying for one another!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another תנא, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and immediately shows why he does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says a גוי only causes a prohibition when two Jews live in the same courtyard and would forbid each other. Here the two Jews live in different courtyards, so they do not forbid each other in that way. Under his view, there should be no prohibition at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what? (introduces another option to test)
They forbid carrying for one another

phrases.english: Rather, what?
Is it like Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov?
But didn't he say:
not unless there are two Jews
who forbid carrying for one another!
phrases.notes: The two Jews here live in separate courtyards, so this condition is not met.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי, כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having rejected רבי מאיר, it tests another תנא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that רב follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires two Jews in one courtyard who forbid each other, which is not the case here.

steps.title: Suggestion: רב follows רבי עקיבא's rule of the foot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רב follows רבי עקיבא. The inner Jew may carry in his own courtyard, but he passes through the outer one, so he forbids carrying there. The next step challenges this proposal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי עקיבא, who said: a foot that is permitted in its own place forbids carrying in a place that is not its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a new answer: רב follows רבי עקיבא. The next step challenges this answer, and step 12 refines it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner Jew is allowed to carry in his own courtyard, as רב said. However, he has a right to walk through the outer courtyard to get out, and he has no עירוב with the Jew there, so his "foot" forbids carrying in the outer courtyard. That would explain both of רב's rulings, but it makes the גוי seem unnecessary, as the next step points out.

keyTerms.meaning: A "foot" (a resident's right to pass through) that is permitted in its own place
Forbids carrying in a place that is not its own

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's rule is that a foot permitted in its own place forbids carrying in a place that is not its own. The גמרא brings this rule as a proposal for רב's ruling, and the next steps refine it.
steps.confusionAlert: "רֶגֶל" (foot) here does not mean a literal foot. It means a person's right to walk through another courtyard.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like Rabbi Akiva, who said:
A foot that is permitted in its own place
phrases.notes: The inner Jew may carry in his own courtyard.

phrases.english: forbids carrying not in its own place.
phrases.notes: His right to pass through the outer courtyard forbids carrying there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּאָמַר: רֶגֶל הַמּוּתֶּרֶת בִּמְקוֹמָהּ אוֹסֶרֶת שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, it gives the תנא who fits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא does רב's ruling follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא: a foot permitted in its own place forbids in another place.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's principle seems to explain why the inner Jew may carry and the outer Jew may not. Step 11 challenges this, and step 12 refines it.

steps.title: Why does רב need a גוי at all?
steps.stepSummary: If רב follows רבי עקיבא, the Jew in the inner courtyard should forbid the outer courtyard on his own. So why mention a גוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a גוי? Even a Jew alone should also forbid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave in Step 10. If רב follows רבי עקיבא, the גוי in רב's case seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, a person who has a right to walk through a courtyard forbids carrying there. So the Jew in the inner courtyard already forbids the outer courtyard, even with no גוי present. Yet רב's case is built around a גוי, so this explanation of רב seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A challenge that a detail looks unnecessary
Even a Jew would also do the same

phrases.english: Why do I need a gentile?
phrases.notes: This refers to the גוי in רב's case.

phrases.english: Even a Jew alone would also forbid!
phrases.notes: Under רבי עקיבא, the inner Jew's path through the outer courtyard is enough to forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי גּוֹי? אֲפִילּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Step 10 that רב follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב follows רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי עקיבא, the inner Jew's right to pass through already forbids the outer courtyard. That makes the גוי in רב's case an unneeded detail.

steps.title: רב follows both opinions, and the Jews made an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says that רב follows both רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי עקיבא. The case is where the Jews made an עירוב, so only the גוי forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: Really, רב follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and also רבי עקיבא. What case are we dealing with here? A case where the Jews made an עירוב together. The only reason it is forbidden is that there is a גוי, and he forbids. If there were no גוי, it would not be forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers the question from Step 11. He explains that רב follows both רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי עקיבא, and that the case involves an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two Jews made an עירוב, they do not forbid each other. That answers why a Jew alone would not be enough. What still forbids is the גוי. From רבי עקיבא we learn that the inner Jew's path through the outer courtyard links the two Jews, so without an עירוב they would forbid each other. That meets רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's condition that a גוי forbids only where two Jews would forbid one another, which answers the objection in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth. Used to keep an earlier position while explaining it differently
What case are we dealing with here? Introduces a narrower case setting
That they made an עירוב, joining their courtyards so they may carry

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא combining two תנאים so that every detail of רב's case has a purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: The עירוב is between the two Jews only. You cannot make an עירוב with a גוי. You can only rent his rights, so the גוי still forbids.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Really, it follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
phrases.notes: This is about when a גוי forbids: only when there are two Jews.

phrases.english: and it follows Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: This is about a person's path through a courtyard forbidding carrying there.

phrases.english: And what are we dealing with here?
A case where they made an eiruv,
phrases.notes: The two Jews joined together through an עירוב.

phrases.english: and the reason is that there is a gentile who forbids,
but if there is no gentile, it is not forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, וּכְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11 by narrowing the case to one with an עירוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (הכא במאי עסקינן) combined with following two opinions together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי עקיבא the גוי seemed unnecessary, because a Jew alone would forbid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Jews made an עירוב, so they do not forbid each other. Only the גוי forbids. That is why רב mentions him.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks about a גוי in the outer courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks רב about the reverse setup. A Jew and a גוי live in the outer courtyard, and a Jew lives in the inner one. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר asked רב: If a Jew and a גוי live in the outer courtyard, and a Jew lives in the inner one, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי אליעזר asks רב what happens when the גוי lives in the outer courtyard instead of the inner one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גוי lived in the inner courtyard. Now the setup is switched. The question is whether the rabbinic decree that a גוי forbids carrying still applies in this new arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer courtyard, the one that opens to the street
The inner courtyard, whose people walk through the outer one

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer asked Rav:
A Jew and a gentile in the outer courtyard
and a Jew in the inner courtyard, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מֵרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב's case, with the גוי inside, to the reverse case, with the גוי outside.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a גוי living in the outer courtyard forbid carrying, just as he does when he lives in the inner courtyard?

steps.title: Why a גוי in the outer courtyard might not forbid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the side of the question that leans lenient. A Jew living with a גוי in the inner courtyard is common, because the גוי is afraid to harm him. In the outer courtyard the גוי is not afraid, so this living arrangement is rare, and maybe the rabbis made no decree for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is that it is common for a Jew to live that way. The גוי is afraid, and he thinks: Soon the Jew from the outer courtyard will come and ask me, 'Where is the Jew who lived next to you?' But here, the גוי thinks: I will tell him, 'He went out and left.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר's question is a real doubt. It shows why the outer-courtyard case might be more lenient than רב's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis made their decree about a גוי to push Jews away from living with a גוי. A Jew normally will not live alone with a גוי, out of fear for his life. In the inner courtyard the גוי is afraid to harm him, because the outer Jew sees who passes by, so living together there is common and the decree applies. In the outer courtyard the גוי can simply say the Jew walked away, so a Jew will not live there with him. Since that is rare, perhaps the rabbis made no decree for it.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'I will tell him' are the גוי's thoughts, not the Jew's. In the outer courtyard the גוי has an easy excuse, so he is not afraid. That is exactly why a Jew would not live there with him.
steps.whatToRemember: The decree that a גוי forbids carrying applies only to common living arrangements. A Jew commonly lives with a גוי in the inner courtyard, where the גוי is afraid. He rarely lives with a גוי in the outer courtyard, where the גוי has an easy excuse. That is the basis for possibly being lenient.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a general principle. Rabbis usually make decrees for common situations, not rare ones (מילתא דלא שכיחא לא גזרו בה רבנן).

phrases.english: There, the reason is
phrases.notes: "There" means רב's case, where the גוי lives in the inner courtyard.

phrases.english: because it is common that he lives that way,
because the gentile is afraid, and he thinks:
Now the Jew will come and say to me:
phrases.notes: This is the Jew of the outer courtyard.

phrases.english: The Jew who was with you, where is he?
phrases.notes: The outer Jew would know whether the inner Jew ever walked out through his courtyard.

phrases.english: But here, the gentile thinks: I will say to him:
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case where the גוי lives in the outer courtyard.

phrases.english: He went out and went on his way.
phrases.notes: The inner Jew cannot disprove this excuse, so the גוי has nothing to fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם טַעְמָא מִשּׁוּם דִּשְׁכִיחַ דְּדָיַיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the doubt raised in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the decree depend on how common the living arrangement is? If so, the rare outer-courtyard case may have no decree.

steps.title: The strict side: maybe the גוי in the outer courtyard is also afraid
steps.stepSummary: The second side of רבי אליעזר's question: maybe the גוי in the outer חצר is also afraid, because the ישראל from the inner חצר could walk through at any moment and see him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe here too the גוי is afraid, because he thinks: right now the Jew may come and see me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of רבי אליעזר's question, the side that leans strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 we said that a גוי in the outer חצר has nothing to fear, so living together there would be rare and maybe the rabbis made no decree. Now we suggest the opposite. The ישראל of the inner חצר passes through the outer one at times nobody can predict. So the גוי is afraid of being seen, living together there is common, and the decree would apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This opens the second side of a question.

phrases.english: Or perhaps, here too he is afraid,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the outer courtyard, where step 14 said he would not be afraid.

phrases.aramaic: דְּסָבַר: הַשְׁתָּא אָתֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְחָזֵי לִי.
phrases.english: for he thinks: at any moment the Jew may come and see me.
phrases.notes: "The Jew" is the one living in the inner courtyard, who passes through the outer one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא, הָכָא נָמֵי מִירְתַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question by giving the strict side that answers the lenient side in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the גוי in the outer חצר also afraid, so that living together there is common and the decree applies?

steps.title: רב answers with a verse: be strict
steps.stepSummary: רב answers with the פסוק 'Give to a wise man and he will become wiser.' This means we should be strict here too, so carrying is forbidden unless they rent from the גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Give to a wise man, and he will become even wiser.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers רבי אליעזר's question with a פסוק from משלי. The point is that the strict side is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not give a long explanation. He quotes a verse that means: you already understand the reasoning, so take it one step further. The rabbis' decree applies to the outer חצר too, and the ישראלים must rent from the גוי before they may carry.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Give to a wise man and he will become wiser' (משלי ט:ט). Here it means: apply the reasoning further and be strict.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's question is decided strictly. Even when the גוי lives in the outer חצר, he forbids carrying unless the ישראלים rent from him.
steps.confusionAlert: The verse is not just a compliment to the student. It is the actual ruling, and it is a strict one.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב is speaking to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: "Give to a wise man, and he will become even wiser."
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in משלי ט:ט; it means we should be strict here too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תֵּן לְחָכָם וְיֶחְכַּם עוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question of steps 13 to 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Be strict. The גוי in the outer חצר also forbids carrying, so the ישראלים must rent from him.

steps.title: The story at the inn: the tenant is away, the landlord is there
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש and the students of רבי חנינא came to an inn. The גוי tenant was not there, but the גוי landlord was.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש and the students of רבי חנינא happened to come to a certain inn. The tenant was not there, but the landlord was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story that sets up the next question. It describes the situation at the inn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inn had ישראלים and a גוי tenant renting rooms from a גוי landlord. The tenant was away on שבת but might come back and forbid carrying. Only the landlord was there to rent from, and that creates the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They happened to come to a place.
A tenant, the one who rents a room.
A landlord, the one who rents out a room.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish and the students of Rabbi Chanina
happened to come to a certain inn,
phrases.notes: This was on שבת.

phrases.english: and the tenant was not there, but the landlord was there.
phrases.notes: Both the tenant and the landlord were גוים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ וְתַלְמִידֵי דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְהָהוּא פּוּנְדָּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the courtyard question behind and starts a new story about renting rights from a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no ruling here yet. The step sets up the case: the גוי tenant is away and only the גוי landlord is present.

steps.title: Can they rent from the landlord?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask whether they may rent the needed rights from the גוי landlord instead of from the tenant who is away.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: what is the law about renting from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask the actual question that the story set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To carry, the ישראלים need to rent the גוי's rights. The tenant is the one living there, but he is not around. The question is whether renting from the landlord, who owns the room, is good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: From him. Here this means from the landlord.

phrases.english: They said: What is the law about renting from him?
phrases.notes: "Him" means the landlord.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ: מַהוּ לְמֵיגַר מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the question that grows out of the inn story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the ישראלים rent the needed rights from the גוי landlord when the גוי tenant is away?

steps.title: Narrowing the question: only when the landlord can evict the tenant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the question. If the landlord cannot remove the tenant, renting from him clearly does not work. The question is only about a case where he can remove him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever the landlord cannot remove the tenant, you do not need to ask, because we cannot rent from him. When you need to ask is where he can remove him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defining exactly what case the question is about. It is not answering the question yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the landlord cannot evict the tenant, the room belongs to the tenant for now, so only the tenant can rent it out. That case is obvious. The real doubt is when the landlord can remove the tenant whenever he wants, because then the landlord might still count as having control.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove him, to evict him.
You do not need to ask. The case is obvious.
We rent. Here it means we cannot rent.

steps.confusionAlert: The first case, where the landlord cannot evict, is not the question. It is settled that renting from him does not work there. The question is only about a landlord who can evict.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלָא מָצֵי מְסַלֵּיק לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: Anywhere that he cannot remove him,
phrases.notes: "He" is the landlord, and "him" is the tenant.

phrases.english: you need not ask, for we cannot rent from him.
phrases.notes: The room belongs to the tenant for now.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי — הֵיכָא דְּמָצֵי מְסַלֵּיק לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: When you need to ask is where he can remove him.
phrases.notes: This is the real question.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלָא מָצֵי מְסַלֵּיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 18 to the one case that is really in doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the landlord rent out the room when he has the power to evict the tenant?

steps.title: Two sides: can the landlord's power to remove the tenant be enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out both sides of the question. Maybe the landlord can rent out the rights because he can remove the tenant. Or maybe it does not help, because right now he has not removed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Since he is able to remove the tenant, we may rent from him. Or perhaps, for now at least, he has not removed him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible ways to think about renting from a landlord who could remove his tenant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says the landlord still holds some control over the place, because he can evict the tenant. That control would be enough to rent out the rights. Side two says what counts is the present reality: the tenant still lives there, so the place is in the tenant's hands, not the landlord's.

keyTerms.meaning: He is able to remove (evict) the tenant

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. The landlord is the owner who is present. The tenant is the one actually living there, and he is away.

phrases.english: What is the law?
Since he is able to remove [the tenant], we may rent [from him].
Or perhaps, for now at least,
he has not removed him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? כֵּיוָן דְּמָצֵי מְסַלֵּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question that step 19 narrowed down
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the landlord's power to evict give him enough control to rent out the tenant's rights, or does only the present situation count?

steps.title: ריש לקיש: let us rent now and ask later
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש tells the students to rent from the landlord for now. When they reach the Sages in the South, they will ask whether they acted correctly.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to them: Let us rent, and when we reach our teachers in the South, we will ask them.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a practical decision for the moment: go ahead and rent, and check with the Sages later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not settle the question in theory. He acts leniently, because the rules of עירוב are rabbinic and we may be lenient in a doubt about a rabbinic law. He still plans to confirm the ruling with greater authorities.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to them: Let us rent,
and when we arrive at our teachers in the South,
we will ask them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: נִשְׂכּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical response to the question in step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rent from the landlord for now, then confirm with the Sages of the South.

steps.title: רבי אפס approves: you did well to rent
steps.stepSummary: They later asked רבי אפס. He told them they did the right thing by renting from the landlord.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and asked רבי אפס. He said to them: You did well that you rented.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a ruling: renting from the landlord was correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the question from steps 18-20. A landlord who can remove his tenant has enough control that renting the rights from him works.
steps.whatToRemember: When the גוי tenant is away, we may rent the rights from the גוי landlord, as long as the landlord can remove the tenant.

phrases.english: They came and asked Rabbi Afes;
he said to them: You did well that you rented.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ שַׁיַּילּוּ לְרַבִּי אַפָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that ריש לקיש's practical decision was correct
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Renting from a landlord who can evict the tenant is valid.

steps.title: New story: the inn owner arrives on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר יוסף, רבי חייא בר אבא, and רבי אסי came to an inn. The גוי owner of the inn arrived only on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר יוסף, רבי חייא בר אבא, and רבי אסי happened to come to a certain inn. The גוי who owned the inn came on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story to set up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new issue here is timing. Before שבת, there was no גוי there to rent from. He showed up only after שבת began.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר יוֹסֵף וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Yosef and Rabbi Chiya bar Abba
and Rabbi Asi happened to come to a certain inn,
and the gentile owner of the inn came on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר יוֹסֵף וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא וְרַבִּי אַסִּי אִיקְּלַעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, similar story about renting from a גוי, now about timing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the גוי owner becomes available only on שבת.

steps.title: First side: is renting like making an עירוב, which must be done before שבת?
steps.stepSummary: They ask whether they may rent from him on שבת. Maybe renting is like making an עירוב. If so, just as an עירוב must be made while it is still day, renting must also be done before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What is the law about renting from him? Is a renter like one who makes an עירוב? Just as an עירוב is made while it is still day, so too renting must be done while it is still day.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is asked, and the first possible comparison is given, which leads to a strict answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting is what allows the עירוב to work, so it might be treated as part of making the עירוב itself. An עירוב must be set up before שבת. If renting counts as part of it, renting on שבת would be too late.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day (before שבת)

phrases.english: They said: What is the law about renting from him?
Is a renter like one who makes an eruv?
Just as one makes an eruv while it is still day,
so too one rents while it is still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ: מַהוּ לְמֵיגַר מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the question raised by the case in step 23 and gives its first side
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is renting from a גוי treated like making an עירוב, so that it must be done before שבת?

steps.title: Second side: is renting like ביטול רשות, which works even on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe renting is like ביטול רשות, giving up one's rights to the area. If so, just as ביטול רשות works even on שבת, renting also works on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps a renter is like one who gives up his rights. Just as one may give up his rights even on שבת, so too one may rent even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second, lenient side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting does not create a new עירוב. It only removes the גוי as a blocking partner. That is very similar to ביטול רשות, which is allowed on שבת itself. If renting is like that, they could rent from the גוי now.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives up his rights to a domain

steps.confusionAlert: עירוב and ביטול רשות are two different tools. An עירוב joins the residents together and must be made before שבת. ביטול רשות is one person stepping aside, and it can be done on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא שׂוֹכֵר כִּמְבַטֵּל רְשׁוּת דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: Or perhaps a renter is like one who renounces his rights;
just as one renounces rights even on Shabbat,
so too one may rent even on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא שׂוֹכֵר כִּמְבַטֵּל רְשׁוּת דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second, opposite side of the question from step 24
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is renting from a גוי treated like ביטול רשות, so that it may be done even on שבת?
steps.whyThisMatters: How we classify renting decides whether people who forgot, or could not rent before שבת, can still fix the problem on שבת.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בר יוסף: We may rent on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר יוסף rules that they may rent from the גוי on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר יוסף said: Let us rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The first Sage answers the question from steps 24-25. He says they may go ahead and rent from the גוי even though it is already שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 24-25 offered two models: renting is like an עירוב (must be done before שבת) or like ביטול רשות (works on שבת). By saying 'let us rent,' רבי חנינא בר יוסף treats renting like ביטול רשות, which works even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Renting the rights to the area from the non-Jew

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Yosef said:
Let us rent,
phrases.notes: Renting works on שבת, like ביטול רשות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר: נִשְׂכּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question of steps 24-25 by choosing the ביטול רשות side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Renting is permitted on שבת, so it is like ביטול רשות.

steps.title: רבי אסי: We may not rent on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי disagrees and rules that they may not rent on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אסי said: Let us not rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The second Sage gives the opposite answer. He says it is too late to rent now that שבת has begun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי treats renting like an עירוב. An עירוב must be made while it is still day, before שבת, so renting must also be done before שבת. Now there is a real disagreement between the Sages at the inn.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day, before שבת (the time limit for an עירוב)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Asi said:
Let us not rent,
phrases.notes: Renting is like an עירוב, so it must be done before שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר: לֹא נִשְׂכּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the opposite side from step 26 and chooses the עירוב model.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Renting is not permitted on שבת, so it is like an עירוב.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא: Rely on the elder and rent
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא decides that, for now, they will follow the older Sage, רבי חנינא בר יוסף, and rent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to them: Let us rely on the words of the elder (רבי חנינא בר יוסף) and rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The third Sage breaks the tie for the moment. He says they should follow the older Sage and rent from the גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a practical decision for the situation in front of them, not a final ruling on the law. When two Sages disagree, he chooses to follow the senior one, רבי חנינא בר יוסף. That is why the question still goes to רבי יוחנן afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: The words of the elder, meaning the older or senior Sage

steps.confusionAlert: The זקן here is not רבי חייא בר אבא himself. It is רבי חנינא בר יוסף, the Sage who said 'let us rent.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to them:
Let us rely on the words of the elder
phrases.notes: The elder is רבי חנינא בר יוסף.

phrases.english: and rent.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִסְמוֹךְ עַל דִּבְרֵי זָקֵן וְנִשְׂכּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the disagreement of steps 26-27 in practice by siding with step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now they rent on שבת, relying on the senior Sage, but the question is still open for a higher authority.

steps.title: They ask רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Later the Sages bring the question to רבי יוחנן, and he begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and asked רבי יוחנן. He said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The Sages take their question to רבי יוחנן, and the גמרא is preparing for his answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the earlier story in steps 21-22, where students acted first and asked a greater authority later. Here too they ask רבי יוחנן whether relying on רבי חנינא בר יוסף and renting on שבת was correct.

phrases.english: They came and asked Rabbi Yochanan,
he said to them:
phrases.notes: His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ שַׁיַּילוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the temporary decision of step 28 to a higher authority for confirmation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was it correct to rent from the גוי on שבת, which means: is renting like ביטול רשות or like an עירוב?
